newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom share unification possible as prices merge.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom share unification possible as prices merge.

text.p: Domestic shares in Russian natural gas group Gazprom, which has a two-tier system for foreign and domestic shares, could eventually rise to the level of foreign traded shares, allowing Russia to consider uniting the two markets, a deputy fuel and energy minister said on Wednesday.
"There is a lot of talk now about uniting the markets... but to unite these markets now would be harmful to Gazprom," Boris Brezdin told Reuters.

"When the moment comes that Gazprom has sold its nine percent, and that will not happen quickly, the situation will change," he said. "We will be able to look into the question of whether to open the market or not."

Brezdin, who is in charge of property issues for the ministry, including natural monopolies, said domestic shares would probably rise to the price level of foreign-traded shares after the sale of nine percent.
Gazprom and the state have limited foreign ownership in Gazprom to that stake.

"When the nine percent is sold, the prices on the domestic market will grow, clearly with some fluctuations, but the internal price will rise," he said, hopefully to the level of the American Depositary Share, which trades abroad.
Gazprom has strongly defended the two-tier system of shares, by which American Depositary Shares, each covering 10 local shares, are traded on Western markets at a three-fold premium.
One percent of Gazprom shares are so far covered by the ADSs, which see wide price swings when rumours of share unification are heeded by the market.
Gazprom had risen to $0.616 at 1345 GMT on the Russian Trading System from $0.600 at the close on Tuesday, while the ADS in London had fallen to $18.30 from $18.80 on Tuesday.
